rules.probability: (S + 1) / (S + C + 2); S = verified supporting investigations, C = contradicting + 0.5 × qualifying

theories.title: Gas-Liquid Two-Phase Pressure Drop and Flow Regimes in Porous Packed Bed Reactors
theories.hypothesis: Simultaneous flow of gases and liquids through porous packed beds in microgravity is governed by capillary forces, liquid hold-up, and packing wettability, with gravitational body forces rendered negligible. It is hypothesized that pressure drop across the packed bed follows a modified Ergun equation incorporating surface tension and contact angle parameters. Furthermore, phase distribution and transition boundaries between bubble, slug, and annular flow regimes depend exclusively on gas and liquid superficial velocities and pore geometry.
theories.summary: Packed bed reactor two-phase pressure drop and flow regimes in microgravity are governed by capillary forces, wettability, and phase velocities.

experiment.title: Packed Bed Reactor Hydrodynamics Module
experiment.design: Pump water and air simultaneously through a fixed column packed with spherical alumina or hydrophilic beads across a wide matrix of gas and liquid flow rates. Record pressure drop across multiple axial taps and capture flow regime transitions using high-speed optical imaging and differential pressure transducers.

theories.title: Suppression of Buoyancy-Driven Convection and Its Effect on Ostwald Ripening and Dendritic Coarsening Kinetics
theories.hypothesis: In the absence of gravitational body forces, natural convection and sedimentation are eliminated, allowing multiphase solid-liquid mixtures to undergo purely diffusion-controlled coarsening. This environment enables the experimental validation of classical Lifshitz, Slyozov, and Wagner (LSW) scaling laws and phase-field crystal models without convective disturbances. It is hypothesized that particle size distributions and temporal power law amplitudes will deviate from terrestrial benchmarks due to the dominance of pure multi-particle diffusion and capillary-driven interface motion. Microgravity removes fluid stirring, which isolates the intrinsic kinetics of topological transitions and morphological evolution in dendritic networks.
theories.summary: Microgravity eliminates buoyancy-driven convection, enabling purely diffusion-controlled coarsening in solid-liquid mixtures to test LSW scaling and phase-field models.

experiment.title: Isothermal Solid-Liquid Coarsening Cell
experiment.design: Process binary metal alloy samples (such as Pb-Sn or W-Ni-Cu) in an isothermal transparent cell on the International Space Station. Subject the samples to controlled temperature plateaus to initiate solid-liquid coexistence, maintaining a strictly quiescent environment over extended durations. Use high-resolution optical and confocal imaging to record temporal changes in topological features, particle size distributions, and interfacial morphologies.

theories.title: Diffusion-Controlled Kinetics and Radical Soot Formation in Non-Buoyant Diffusion Flames
theories.hypothesis: In microgravity, the suppression of buoyancy-induced convective flows leads to significantly increased residence times, altered scalar dissipation rates, and expanded flame structures in laminar diffusion flames. It is hypothesized that these extended residence times promote enhanced nucleation, condensation, and coagulation of soot precursors, resulting in larger soot particle sizes and modified soot volume fractions compared to terrestrial flames. Consequently, flame extinction limits are governed primarily by radiative heat loss and chemical kinetics rather than forced convective strain.
theories.summary: Soot particle growth and flame extinction limits are altered in microgravity due to extended residence times and suppressed buoyancy-induced convection.

experiment.title: Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame Soot and Extinction Cell
experiment.design: Establish steady spherical or coflow laminar diffusion flames of ethylene or methane on a porous circular burner within a combustion chamber. Dilute the fuel and oxidizer streams with varying fractions of nitrogen and helium at controlled ambient pressures. Measure temperature fields, flame dimensions, and soot volume fractions using thin filament pyrometry and laser scattering diagnostics.

theories.title: Thermocapillary and Marangoni Convection in Free-Surface Fluid Systems
theories.hypothesis: In the absence of gravity-driven buoyancy, surface tension gradients along fluid-fluid or liquid-gas interfaces dominate transport phenomena, driving vigorous thermocapillary and Marangoni convection. This surface-driven flow directly couples thermal boundary layers, free-surface deformation, and velocity fields, triggering oscillatory flow instabilities at critical Marangoni numbers. Without gravitational stabilization, these flows significantly alter heat transfer rates, interface shapes, and pore mobility during solidification.
theories.summary: Surface tension gradients drive dominant thermocapillary and Marangoni flows in microgravity, dictating oscillatory instabilities and interfacial heat transfer.

support.title: DEvice for the study of Critical LIquids and Crystallization Directional Solidification Insert-Reflight
support.datum: The study evaluates how directional solidification parameters influence interface shapes and microstructures.
support.quote: The dynamics and stability of cellular and dendritic growth patterns, and the relationship between the tip geometry and growth pattern were also to be investigated

support.title: Development and Verification of a 3D Nucleate Pool Boiling Simulation Model Using PSI Data
support.datum: The study models vapor bubble dynamics and heat transfer processes under microgravity conditions.
support.quote: The verified model can be used to further study scenarios not investigated on ISS such as vapor bubble departure and collapse.

support.title: Electrically Driven Liquid Film Flow Boiling in the Absence of Gravity
support.datum: The study examines fluid flow mechanisms necessary to manage vapor bubble removal and heat transfer in microgravity boiling.
support.quote: Boiling is not acceptable in the absence of gravity unless the generated vapor bubbles can be expelled from the boiling surface and fresh liquid can be pumped onto the hot surface through some mechanism.

theories.title: Polydispersity-Driven Coarsening and Delayed Collapse in Colloidal Gels
theories.hypothesis: In colloidal suspensions and gels, particle polydispersity and non-adsorbing polymer depletants introduce structural frustration that alters phase separation kinetics and mechanical stability. It is hypothesized that in microgravity—free from sedimentation and gravitational collapse—aging proceeds through systematic coarsening and thermal fluctuation damping over hours to days. Polydispersity in particle size introduces order-of-magnitude variations in the time scale of gel collapse, governed by the interplay of critical Casimir forces and local structural rearrangements.
theories.summary: Polydispersity and depletants control the aging, structural coarsening, and delayed collapse timescales of colloidal gels in microgravity.

experiment.title: Advanced Colloids Confocal Microscopy Cell
experiment.design: Prepare aqueous suspensions of polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) colloids with controlled size polydispersity and varying concentrations of polymer depletant inside a temperature-regulated sample cell. Subject the samples to precise thermal quenches aboard the ISS and observe 3D structural evolution over time using a high-resolution confocal microscope.

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment- Microscopy
support.datum: The document investigates how particle polydispersity affects the collapse time and coarsening dynamics of colloidal gels in microgravity.
support.quote: Previous Earth-based experiments show that polydispersity dramatically affects the time it takes for these gels to collapse. The imaging goal was to observe crystallites and resolve particle centroid positions with less than 20% error. Hypothesis: Polydispersity significantly affects the time scale and dynamics of coarsening. It is believed that polydispersity can lead to a substantial difference in the collapse time of weak gels

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment - Temperature 6
support.datum: The document provides evidence and hypotheses on how polydispersity introduces order-of-magnitude variations in weak gel collapse timescales.
support.quote: It is hypothesized that polydispersity in the polymer makes order-of-magnitude differences in the time scale of collapse of weak gels. The investigation attempts to make benchmark microgravity measurements and advance theories that allow a more comprehensive understanding of the role of polydispersity in the coarsening process.

support.title: Binodal Colloidal Aggregation Test - 4
support.datum: The document explores the effects of particle polydispersity on colloidal systems in microgravity.
support.quote: BCAT-4-Poly will use model hard-spheres (suspended in a liquid that makes them transparent) to explore pure and seeded colloidal crystal nucleation and the effects of polydispersity, providing insight into how to understand and control the processes used by nature to bring order out of disorder.

support.title: Binary Colloidal Alloy Test - 6
support.datum: The document investigates crystal growth in systems with varying particle sizes.
support.quote: Seeded Growth (BCAT-6-Seeded Growth): to build on previous research looking at how dense groups of particles may be coaxed to form crystal structures when much larger “seed” particles are added.

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment - Temperature Control and Gradient Sample 11
support.datum: The document studies crystal nucleation and growth by varying particle and depletant sizes in microgravity.
support.quote: Objectives included study of nucleation and growth of crystals within colloidal samples by varying the size and concentration of colloids and depletant, exploring the effect of temperature gradients, and demonstrating control of particle shape and density

support.title: Physics of Colloids in Space
support.datum: The document investigates colloid-polymer mixtures and depletion-induced interactions forming gel-like structures.
support.quote: In addition, the structure and dynamics of gel-like structures formed by colloid-polymer mixtures will be measured using static and dynamic light scattering and the ultimate equilibrium structures behavior of the mixture will be determined.

support.title: Phase Transitions in Colloid-Polymer Mixtures in Microgravity
support.datum: The document explores how non-adsorbing polymer depletion interactions alter phase separation kinetics in microgravity.
support.quote: Specifically, the research sought to determine how depletion interactions, arising from non-adsorbing polymers, influence the kinetics and morphology of phase separation and crystallization in complex fluids.

support.title: Colloidal gels: Aging in microgravity, Structure of highly polydisperse gels
support.datum: The document directly confirms that colloidal gels coarsen in microgravity and that particle polydispersity and large particles structure gel connectivity.
support.quote: Project 1: Colloidal gels in microgravity conditions will coarsen over time, and their thermal fluctuations will diminish over time as the gel gets coarser; the coarsening will continue indefinitely because gravitational collapse will not be possible. Project 2: Large particles play significant roles in highly polydisperse colloidal gels, as they serve as highly connected nodes in the structure.

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment-Temperature 4
support.datum: The document shows how structural frustration introduced by particle dopants alters crystal and gel properties.
support.quote: The experiments introduced disorder by added colloidal dopants into the samples; these dopants introduce structural frustration into the crystals which, in turn, can transform the crystals into disordered solids (polycrystalline) and glasses with novel mechanical properties.

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment-Microscopy 2 Reflight
support.datum: The document examines phase behavior and colloidal interactions near critical points in microgravity.
support.quote: ACE-M2R observes the microscopic behavior of liquids and gases separating from each other. The investigation examines the behavior of model (colloid rich) liquids and model (colloid poor) gases near the critical point

support.title: Coarsening in Solid Liquid Mixtures-2
support.datum: The document investigates coarsening kinetics in mixtures, removing sedimentation via microgravity.
support.quote: The theory of coarsening has been described by Lifshitz, Slyozov and Wagner (LSW) predicts that for the limit of zero volume fraction particles grow with time as the cube root of the average radius

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment -Temperature controlled- 2
support.datum: The document studies self-assembly and tunable particle interactions driven by critical Casimir forces in microgravity.
support.quote: By studying this process based on critical Casimir forces in microgravity, where sedimentation and convection are essentially removed, we will learn how to adjust complex attractive particle interactions.

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment-Temperature 5
support.datum: The document examines interparticle interactions and their impact on rheology and mechanical stability in particulate suspensions.
support.quote: The overarching goal of the project was to gain a better fundamental understanding of the relationship between bijel morphology, rheology, mechanical stability, and processability through combined ground-based and microgravity experiments

support.title: Coarsening in Solid-Liquid Mixtures-2 Reflight
support.datum: The document examines solid-liquid mixture coarsening dynamics in microgravity.
support.quote: The theory of coarsening has been described by Lifshitz, Slyozov and Wagner (LSW) predicts that for the limit of zero volume fraction particles grow with time as the cube root of the average radius

theories.title: Colloidal Self-Assembly and Crystallization via Tunable Interparticle Potentials
theories.hypothesis: Under microgravity conditions where sedimentation is effectively eliminated, colloidal suspensions interacting via tunable repulsive, depletion, or critical Casimir forces self-assemble into highly ordered 3D superlattices and complex crystal structures. The kinetics of nucleation and growth in these systems are governed exclusively by Brownian motion and short-range potential wells. Introducing structural dopants or temperature gradients induces controlled phase transitions between crystalline, polycrystalline, and glassy states.
theories.summary: Sedimentation-free microgravity enables pristine self-assembly of colloidal structures and precise study of crystallization kinetics via tunable interparticle forces.

experiment.title: Critical Casimir Colloidal Assembly Assay
experiment.design: Suspend silica or polymer microspheres in a binary solvent mixture inside temperature-controlled sample cells. Adjust local temperatures around the binary consolute boundary to reversibly tune critical Casimir attractions while recording 3D particle positions with confocal microscopy.

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment - Temperature 1
support.datum: Microgravity eliminates sedimentation and enables unhindered colloidal particles to form networks and structures.
support.quote: Observing colloidal interactions without the influence of gravity provides new insight into how unhindered particles form network and structures.

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment - Temperature 7
support.datum: Under microgravity, particles self-organize into crystals with depletion forces, and temperature gradients induce crystallite formation.
support.quote: It is hypothesized that under certain conditions, the particles should self-organize into crystals with simple cubic symmetry, which is set by the size of the nano-size depletant. Increasing particle number density using a temperature gradient, i.e., thermophoresis, is expected to induce formation of crystallites.

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment with Temperature Control - R [Ellipsoid]
support.datum: Ellipsoidal colloidal suspensions under microgravity and temperature gradients form self-assembled 3D structures.
support.quote: The objective of the ACE-TR (Ellipsoid) experiment was to image and document the self-assembly of complex 3D structures formed from small elliptical colloidal particles suspended in a fluid. Temperature gradients were varied with the objective to explore the effect of thermophoresis on colloidal crystallization.

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment - Temperature Control and Gradient Sample 11
support.datum: Microgravity suppresses sedimentation, allowing colloidal particles to exhibit unique crystallization and self-assembly behaviors.
support.quote: Under microgravity conditions, colloidal particles would exhibit unique crystallization and self-assembly behaviors that differ from those observed under Earth's gravity.

support.title: Physics of Hard Spheres Experiment
support.datum: Reducing sedimentation in microgravity allows the study of freezing, melting, and crystal nucleation kinetics governed by Brownian motion.
support.quote: By significantly reducing gravitational sedimentation the primary objective of this microgravity investigation was to quantify the volume fractions at which dispersions of hard spheres freeze, melt, and become glasses; the equilibrium structure associated with each phase; the dynamics of Brownian fluctuations in each phase; the kinetics of the nucleation and growth of the crystalline phase

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment -Temperature controlled- 2
support.datum: Removal of sedimentation in microgravity allows investigation of self-assembly driven by critical Casimir forces.
support.quote: By studying this process based on critical Casimir forces in microgravity, where sedimentation and convection are essentially removed, we will learn how to adjust complex attractive particle interactions.

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment - Imaging, Folding and Assembly of Colloidal Molecules
support.datum: Tuning repulsive and attractive interactions in microgravity leads to the self-assembly of complex 3D structures.
support.quote: Furthermore, by tuning the balance between electric double layer repulsion and hydrophobic attraction on both colloidal dimers and lock-and-key particles, we aim to study the assembly of those colloidal molecules into complex three-dimensional structures and measure the binding equilibrium constants.

support.title: Binary Colloidal Alloy Test - 3
support.datum: Microgravity and depletion forces induced by polymers allow binary alloy colloidal self-assembly without sedimentation.
support.quote: This investigation hypothesizes that by taking advantage of microgravity and avoiding sedimentation binary alloys with very different materials and sizes and by addition of polymers particles to induce attractive forces can lead to exciting and promising form of colloidal engineering to synthesize a new class of materials.

support.title: Binodal Colloidal Aggregation Test - 4
support.datum: Avoiding sedimentation in space enables the observation of colloidal phase transitions, crystallization, and self-organization.
support.quote: Colloidal particles would exhibit behaviors analogous to atoms, allowing the study of phase transitions, crystallization, and self-organization without the interference of sedimentation and convection present on Earth.

support.title: Physics of Colloids in Space
support.datum: Microgravity enables the formation of binary colloidal superlattices and studies of nucleation and growth kinetics.
support.quote: The availability of microgravity will allow binary colloidal superlattices to be formed from different materials providing new insights into the nucleation and growth kinetics of binary colloidal crystal alloy and thereby establish the new field of “colloid engineering.”

support.title: Phase Transitions in Colloid-Polymer Mixtures in Microgravity
support.datum: Depletion interactions from polymers affect phase separation and crystallization kinetics in colloidal mixtures under microgravity.
support.quote: Specifically, the research sought to determine how depletion interactions, arising from non-adsorbing polymers, influence the kinetics and morphology of phase separation and crystallization in complex fluids.

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment-Nanoparticle Haloing
support.datum: Stabilized suspensions form ordered 3D colloidal crystal structures under appropriate conditions.
support.quote: When NPH suspensions were allowed to settle under gravity, those that were stabilized (while in suspension) formed highly ordered, 3-dimensional colloidal crystal structures.

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment - Aging Dynamics and Stress-Relaxation in Colloidal Gels Studied in Microgravity
support.datum: Thermo-reversible colloidal suspensions exhibit structural dynamics and restructuring behaviors in microgravity.
support.quote: ACE-T10 delivered unique insights into the restructuring behavior of thermo-reversible colloidal gels, a topic of noticeable interest for the community of scientists dealing with soft materials.

support.title: Binary Colloidal Alloy Test - 5
support.datum: Microgravity eliminates sedimentation, permitting the study of colloidal crystallization, phase transitions, and self-organization.
support.quote: Colloidal particles would exhibit behaviors analogous to atoms, allowing the study of phase transitions, crystallization, and self-organization without the interference of sedimentation and convection present on Earth.

support.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment-Temperature 5
support.datum: Interparticle interactions and forces at the colloidal scale heavily influence the structuring of particle suspensions in microgravity.
support.quote: This investigation hypothesizes that interparticle interactions have a profound impact on the rheology of bijel particulate suspensions and attempts to answer the fundamental scientific question as to how the various forces at the colloidal scale are affected by Marangoni convection in microgravity.

support.title: Binary Colloidal Alloy Test - 6
support.datum: Absence of sedimentation and convection facilitates the study of colloidal self-organization and phase behavior.
support.quote: Colloidal particles would exhibit behaviors analogous to atoms, allowing the study of phase transitions, crystallization, and self-organization without the interference of sedimentation and convection present on Earth.

against.title: Advanced Colloids Experiment-Temperature 4
against.datum: Sample degradation prior to the experiment led to gelation instead of crystallization, providing insights into gels rather than crystals.
against.quote: The originally planned experiments were no longer possible due to gelation, but the ACE-T4 experiment based on the changed samples (gels) provided qualitatively different insights into the behavior of 3D colloidal gels over a range of temperatures and temperature gradients.
